column11: derived: Pfizer generated $23,703mm of free cash flow on $185,759mm of revenue over 2023, 2024 and 2025, a 12.76% margin, against the 33.8% its cost of sales, SG&A and R&D leave. The 2021 and 2022 COVID years are excluded because a 36% margin on a vaccine windfall is not what this company earns. Restated before interest: PFE paid $8,181mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 4.40% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 22.18% to 17.77%. Checked at replacement capex: no plant depreciation on file for every year, and no amortisation line to take it out of the combined figure, so the charge stands. Restated without one-off cash: PFE's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried $1,350mm of deal payments in operating cash flow, capital allocation whose assets the book values separately; $63mm of legal settlements; $4,400mm of US transition tax (2023 instalment 1,000mm; 2024 instalment 1,300mm; 2025 instalment 2,100mm). None recurs, so the charge falls from 17.77% to 14.52%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 PFE's cash flow statement shows receivables up $25mm, inventories up $1,462mm, payables down $1,792mm, a working capital build of $3,279mm, 1.77% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from 14.52% to 12.66%.

column11: lookup.py demand Padcev: CMS Medicare Part B 2024, $641,224,462 over 5,839 beneficiaries = $109,818 per beneficiary
column12: Judgement: house convention, and the same anchor the PF-08046054 seed uses. Padcev is enfortumab vedotin, Pfizer's own vedotin ADC from the Seagen platform, given with pembrolizumab in first line, which matches this regimen. No Datroway or other lung ADC CMS row is on file. The case against: Padcev's figure is in urothelial cancer, not lung, and an add-on to pembrolizumab in a PD-L1-high population that already does well on pembrolizumab alone may be priced lower. The price covers sigvotatug vedotin only, not the pembrolizumab backbone

column11: Social Security Act section 1847A: Medicare Part B pays 106% of average sales price, and ASP is net of manufacturer volume, prompt-pay and cash discounts, chargebacks and rebates (1847A(c)(3); CMS Part B drug payment guidance), so the manufacturer's net is the CMS figure divided by 1.06, 5.66% below it. The book's own statement of the convention is backend/gross_to_net.py (Part B 'deduction there is the 6% add-on'), and the PF-08046054, ABBV-1480, PF-08634404 and sacituzumab tirumotecan seeds carry 0.0566 on Part B anchors
column12: Direction checked: 0.0566 off list, so net is 0.109818 x 0.9434 = $103,602 per patient-year. The 0.5 convention was measured on nine Part D drugs against their IRA negotiated prices and does not apply to a Part B price, which is already net. The case against: ASP excludes Medicaid section 1927 rebates and 340B ceiling prices, both material in oncology infusion, so the true net sits somewhat below this; and Part B spending per beneficiary is below a full year of therapy, which the 0.5 convention partly offset and this one does not

column11: KEYNOTE-024 (Reck et al., N Engl J Med 2016, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1606774): median PFS 10.3 months on pembrolizumab alone in untreated advanced NSCLC with PD-L1 TPS of 50% or more, the control arm and population of SigVie-003
column12: Constant hazard from a median: 1 - 0.5^(12/10.3) = 0.554, the form the ABBV-1480 and PF-08046054 seeds use (the brief's 1 - exp(-12/10.3) gives 0.688 but treats the median as a mean). The case against: no first-line median for the combination has been published; the combination is designed to extend PFS, which would lower this, while vedotin toxicity (neuropathy) can end the ADC before progression, which would raise it. The only published median for the molecule is 3.6 months in previously treated NSCLC (Peters et al., J Clin Oncol 2026, doi:10.1200/JCO-25-02016), a later line and not this setting

column11: NCT06758401 (SigVie-003) primary completion 2028-09-05 (ClinicalTrials.gov, last update 2026-07-22)
column12: Launch is clearly later than 2027. A readout in late 2028, a filing in 2029 and a launch in late 2029 make 2030 the first full year, the book's convention of two calendar years after primary completion (the PF-08046054 seed). Judgement on the review timeline. The earlier Phase 3, SigVie-002 (NCT06012435), missed its OS primary endpoint in the overall population (Pfizer press release, 22 June 2026, pfizer.com/news/press-release/press-release-detail/pfizer-announces-topline-phase-3-results-sigvotatug-vedotin), so it provides no earlier launch; Pfizer cited a stronger trend after one prior line but no filing was announced

column12: SigVie-003 enrols first-line locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with TPS of 50% or more, both histologies. The case against: PD-L1-high and driver-positive status are not independent (driver-positive tumours are less often PD-L1 high), so multiplying slightly understates; and the 32.8% is per test, not per patient

column11: EV+P, enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab, reached 51% of US first-line la/mUC patients in 2024, its first full year (Flatiron, ASCO GU 2026, as recorded in the book's vepugratinib seed)
column12: Judgement: half of the measured incumbent. EV+P is the closest measured analogue, a Pfizer vedotin ADC added to pembrolizumab in first line, but it replaced platinum chemotherapy after doubling overall survival; sigvotatug vedotin would be added to an already effective pembrolizumab monotherapy, its monotherapy Phase 3 missed OS, and first-line PD-L1-high NSCLC is contested by chemo-immunotherapy and PD-1xVEGF bispecifics. The halving is not measured. The case for higher: if SigVie-003 hits both PFS and OS, an add-on to pembrolizumab is an easy switch, as EV+P showed. The case for lower: the PF-08046054 seed takes 0.25 against docetaxel in second line, where the displaced therapy is weaker
